title: Mulligatawny with Chicken, Red Lentils and Coconut
summary: A warming, gently spiced soup of chicken, red lentils, carrots and apple, cooked with mustard seeds, turmeric and cumin and finished with coconut milk and lime. Thick, golden and satisfying enough for a main course.
equipment: large casserole or heavy pot (at least 5 litres) with a lid

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
large tart green apple, peeled, cored and chopped
boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Heat the oil in the casserole over medium-high heat, add the onion and 0.5 tsp salt, and cook for about 8 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent. The salt draws out moisture so the onion softens evenly without scorching.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.text: Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes, until fragrant. Tip in the mustard seeds, turmeric, curry powder, cayenne and cumin seeds and stir constantly for about 90 seconds, until the mustard seeds begin to pop. Frying spices in oil releases flavour compounds that only dissolve in fat, giving a deeper, rounder taste.

steps.title: Add vegetables and flour
steps.text: Stir in the carrots, celery and apple and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tomato purée, then the flour, and cook for 2 minutes more, stirring so everything is evenly coated. Cooking the flour briefly removes its raw taste and later helps thicken the soup smoothly.

steps.title: Simmer until thick
steps.text: Add the chicken, lentils, broth, water and 0.5 tsp salt and bring to the boil, scraping up anything stuck to the base. Reduce to a simmer, cover for 10 minutes, then uncover and simmer for 15-20 minutes more, stirring often, until the lentils collapse and the chicken reaches 74 °C. The red lentils break down completely, giving the soup its creamy body without any blending.

steps.title: Finish with coconut
steps.text: Stir in the coconut milk and heat through without letting it boil hard, then add the lime juice. Taste, add a splash of water if it is very thick, and serve scattered with coriander. Lime added at the end keeps its fresh sharpness to cut through the richness.

tips: Have all the spices measured before you start, as they need less than 2 minutes in the hot oil.
A common mistake is not stirring once the lentils go in; they settle and stick to the base, so scrape the bottom every few minutes.
The soup thickens as it stands, so loosen leftovers with a little water when reheating.
A spoonful of plain yoghurt on top adds a cool contrast.
storage: Cool and refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat gently, stirring and adding a splash of water, until piping hot (74 °C) throughout. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
